To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the more the civil servants are exposed to the performance audit, the more negative they are towards it.
the ministries’ responses to the performance audits of the SAIs are negative, especially among top executives, and that the ministries’ reactions are stronger than the agencies’ reactions.

1) civil servants in ministries are less positive to performance audits than civil servants in agencies; 2) top executives are less positive than middle managers and others; and 3) civil servants more exposed (i.e. with more experience) to performance audit are more critical to performance audit.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether performance audit has the intended effect on public administration.
the relationship between performance audit and resistance.
how civil servants perceive and react to the SAIs’ control, and how this perception and reactions vary between the ministries and agencies, and among different civil servants.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the more control the more resistance.
civil servants in ministries, top civil servants and civil servants exposed to performance audit, are less positive to SAIs’ control than other civil servants.
civil servants are less positive towards control when they are subject to control themselves.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
civil servants in Norway are more negative to performance audit than expected.
civil servants are not particularly positive to performance audit, and that the more exposed to performance audits, the more negative they become.
the ministries and agencies’ responses were mixed and that they varied across different groups of civil servants.
The main takeaway from our work is that
performance audit is a double edged sword.
the ministries’ and their employees’ reactions to performance audits seem to be more negative than those in the agencies.
the ministries and agencies’ reactions to control are not uniform.
